title: Build a world beyond the frame.
summary: Turn a simple idea into a cinematic scene. Start with the subject. Make the atmosphere your own.

variables.label: Setting
variables.default: an unfamiliar planet with distant mountains

variables.label: Lighting
variables.default: warm side light against a cool atmosphere

steps.title: Start with a reference
steps.description: Upload a photograph you own or have permission to use. A reference is optional; your subject and setting can carry the composition.

steps.title: Make it yours
steps.description: Change the subject, setting, lighting, and aspect ratio below. Specific choices lead to a clearer brief.

steps.title: Generate and refine
steps.description: Copy the finished prompt into your image tool with your reference attached. Review details, then request one focused change at a time.

prompt: Create an original cinematic editorial image featuring {{subject}} in {{setting}}. Use {{lighting}} lighting, a wide sense of scale, layered depth, and realistic surface textures. Preserve a clear focal point, leave space for a title, and use a {{ratio}} composition. Use the attached image only as a compositional reference; do not reproduce its characters, logos, or title.

title: Make the everyday look extraordinary.
summary: A considered product scene, with tactile materials and light that does the talking.
prompt: Create a studio product photograph of {{product}} on a matte {{surface}} surface. Use soft natural light from one side, gentle shadows, and a quiet monochromatic backdrop. Emphasize authentic material texture, clear product proportions, and generous negative space. No invented logos or labels. Composition: {{ratio}}.

title: From open tabs to a clear point of view.
summary: A repeatable workflow for turning a messy research question into an evidence-led brief.

variables.label: Research question
variables.default: how small teams can evaluate a new tool

steps.title: Define the decision
steps.description: State what the research should help someone decide. Include context, constraints, and the audience.
steps.prompt: Help me scope this research: {{topic}}. Ask up to three questions that would change the recommendation.

steps.title: Build an evidence map
steps.description: Collect primary sources. Keep the author, publication date, URL, and a short note on what each source establishes.
steps.prompt: Create an evidence table for {{topic}}. Columns: claim, primary source, date, support, uncertainty. Mark anything you could not verify.

steps.title: Write the brief
steps.description: Turn the evidence into a useful point of view, with a recommendation and its limits.
steps.prompt: Use the evidence map to write a brief for {{audience}}. Lead with the decision, then explain the reasoning, counterargument, and remaining unknowns.

prompt: Research {{topic}} for {{audience}}. Begin by listing the questions that matter. Find primary sources, preserve source dates and links, and separate direct evidence from interpretation. Compare conflicting findings. Deliver a one-page brief with a recommendation, the strongest counterargument, evidence gaps, and the next useful question. Do not invent citations.

title: Give your best ideas room to grow.
summary: A practical focus exercise: choose what matters, and give it your attention.

variables.label: What are you working toward?
variables.default: my current learning and work goals

steps.title: Get it out of your head
steps.description: Write down the goals competing for your attention. Include professional and personal commitments.

steps.title: Choose your five
steps.description: Review which priorities matter most now. Consider time, value, and whether the goal is yours or simply expected of you.

steps.title: Create a not-now list
steps.description: Keep other ideas somewhere safe. Revisit them at a planned review instead of switching priorities every day.

prompt: Help me prioritize {{goals}}. Ask about my values, deadlines, and current commitments. Group related goals, identify the five most valuable priorities, and suggest a realistic next action for each. Put everything else on a clearly labeled not-now list. Explain the tradeoffs without claiming certainty.
body: The 5/25 exercise is a prioritization framework often attributed to Warren Buffett. Its origin is not established here; the useful part is the act of choosing a small set of priorities.
The goal is not to turn every hour into work. It is to spend attention deliberately, and leave room for rest, curiosity, and changing circumstances.

title: Design with a little more intention.
summary: Build a clear editorial layout with a strong headline, breathing room, and a simple hierarchy.
prompt: Design a {{format}} about {{topic}}. Use a charcoal background, white typography, a bold condensed headline, and a rounded readable body font. Establish one focal image and a consistent grid. Keep generous margins, avoid decorative gradients and glows, and preserve clear contrast. Supply a layout plan and exact copy before generating imagery.

title: Learn it. Use it. Make it stick.
summary: A learning plan built around practice and feedback, rather than another pile of saved tabs.

variables.label: Time available
variables.default: 20 minutes a day for two weeks

prompt: Help me learn {{skill}} in {{time}}. Start with a short diagnostic of my current level. Build a plan around practical exercises, worked examples, feedback, and spaced recall. Each session should end with something I can do, not just read. Adjust the plan when I show you my work.

title: A better website starts with a better brief.
summary: Move from idea to a testable page with a small, clear set of prompts.

steps.title: Write the brief
steps.description: Describe the audience, their main task, your content, and what successful use looks like.
steps.prompt: Help me define {{project}}. Identify its primary audience, three core user journeys, a content model, and what can wait until later. Ask only for details that affect the implementation.

steps.title: Build the first working flow
steps.description: Start with one complete journey. Make the actual interactions work before adding more pages.
steps.prompt: Implement the main journey for {{project}} with responsive navigation, accessible controls, useful empty states, and clear feedback. Use sample data labeled as sample data. Explain any missing service connections.

steps.title: Test on a phone
steps.description: Check the actual page at a narrow width. Try copying, saving, uploading, and navigating with the keyboard.
steps.prompt: Test {{project}} at 390px and 1440px. Verify navigation, text readability, focus order, forms, and loading or error states. Fix failures and report what was actually checked.

title: The Origin Edit: make room for better ideas.
summary: One practical prompt, one useful workflow, and one idea to carry into your week.
body: Welcome to The Origin Edit. This is a quieter corner of the internet for people who want to make useful things, think a little more clearly, and stay curious.
TRY THIS — Before asking a tool to produce something, describe the audience, the purpose, and what a good result looks like. A useful brief is often a better starting point than a clever phrase.
A WORKFLOW WORTH KEEPING — Start with one question. Gather a small set of reliable sources. Write down what each source actually establishes. Only then ask for a summary or a recommendation.
ONE IDEA TO TAKE WITH YOU — A saved resource is a possibility, not progress. Pick one thing from your library this week and put it to work.
Until next time, keep exploring. — AI Tech Origin
